chunks: Rijal al-Najashi: From our Shaykh al-Mufid in his book Masabih al-Nur: reported to me Ibn Qulawayh, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Abdallah ibn Ja'far, from Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari who said:

I presented to Abu Muhammad, the Master of al-Askari (peace be upon him), the book 'Yawm wa Layla' of Yunus, so he said to me: Who authored this? I said: It is authored by Yunus, the client of the family of Yaqtin, he said: May Allah give him for every letter a light on the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْعَسْكَرِ: The Master of al-Askari (Imam al-Hasan al-Askari)
key_terms.مَوْلَى آلِ يَقْطِينَ: Client/Free-man of the family of Yaqtin
key_terms.يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ: A specific book title, 'A Day and a Night'

ai.seo_question: What was the Imam's response when presented with Yunus's book Yawm wa Layla?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted via the renowned scholar al-Mufid, highlights the high status of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a prominent companion of the Imams, affirming the spiritual merit of preserving and transmitting knowledge. The Imam’s specific blessing of 'light for every letter' underscores the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of written tradition and the individual contribution to religious scholarship. It serves as a foundational text for valuing solitary reports (ahad) from truthful narrators, linking textual preservation directly to eschatological reward.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/-] Rijal al-Najashi: From our Shaykh al-Mufid in his book “Masabih al-Nur”: reported to us Ibn Qulawayh from Ali b. al-Husayn b. Babawayh from Abdallah b. Ja’far from Dawud b. al-Qasim al-Ja’fari who said:

I presented the book “Yawm wa Layla” of Yunus to Abi Muhammad al-Askari عليه السلام, so he said to me: who authored this? I said: it has been authored by Yunus the client of the family of Yaqtin, he said: may Allah give him for every letter a light on the day of judgment.
